savings.reason: Section 1 distinguishes NEA accrued savings from continued prohibitions on property blocked under EO12722/12724. This may be a continuing independent rule under the later order, not merely accrued rights. Full current regulation and statutory note are needed before choosing a whole-order savings state.

research_rationale: The full original and held actor texts were read. EO12724 section 6 is an actual partial revocation with savings, effective immediately under its section 4; it needs clause-by-clause inconsistency analysis. EO12771 section 1 revokes Kuwaiti orders 12723/12725 and expressly leaves the EO12722 emergency unaffected, so the machine whole-revocation link is not a legal end here. EO12743 invokes military authorities in furtherance of the emergency without a located repeal of EO12722. EO12817 implements asset transfers and protects accrued transfer rights. EO13303 section 2(a) removes specified property from EO12722/12724 and section 2(b) expressly preserves prior administrative measures subject to exceptions. EO13350 revokes EO12722 effective July 30, 2004 at 12:01 a.m. EDT and saves accrued matters while expressly continuing some blocked-property prohibitions. Current 31 CFR 576.201 and 50 USC 1701 note leads may bear directly on residual independence and cutoff status; only snippets are held. They must be acquired and read, not resolved by treating every citation as current law or every nominal revocation as total cessation.

EO12724 section 6 revokes EO12722 only to the extent inconsistent and continues administrative actions under EO12724. A provision-by-provision inconsistency determination is required to establish each first end; a single 2004 revocation date cannot replace this earlier partial scope analysis.

earlier_endings_and_partial_scope: The actual EO12724/13303 partial changes and express EO13350 continuation defeat a blanket same-date first-end assignment. EO12771 is a false-positive target relation. EO13350's explicit section 10 supplies the 2004 effective date, but that is insufficient to resolve earlier first ends or the current-law conflict.
